description: StEER - 3 March 2019 Tornadoes in the Southeastern US: Field Assessment Structural Team (FAST) Early Access Reconnaissance Report (EARR) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by David Roueche, Auburn University (auburn.edu). This Early Access Reconnaissance Report (EARR) summarizes the structural performance of buildings and other structures in the 3 March 2019 tornado outbreak that struck the southeastern United States with at least 34 confirmed tornadoes. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-qav0-t570. Keywords: StEER, Reconnaissance, EARR, tornado, Alabama, Florida. Published 2019-06-04. Facility named: StEER - Structural Engineering Extreme Event Reconnaissance. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
